observations.explanation: The paper describes a modular construction pipeline and a reward-function endpoint that can use interaction history and container state, enabling custom reward designs (PDF p. 4). The interface and appendix also discuss customization and extension (PDF pp. 14–15).

The reported SQL results show Try Again outperforming Single Turn for every listed model, including GPT-4 rising from 9.1% to 73.7% overall; the paper also reports gains in Bash (PDF pp. 6–7). This supports the qualified claim about interaction and benchmark viability.
The paper explicitly states that its implemented environments are limited to Bash and SQL and that the CTF dataset has only four instances, limiting broad evaluation (PDF p. 9; see also PDF p. 26).

The paper describes Docker containers as execution sandboxes, but warns that Bash and SQL impose no strict action-space limitations and that direct sim-to-real transfer may put real systems at risk (PDF pp. 3–4, 26). The claim accurately distinguishes sandboxed evaluation from unestablished deployment safety.
